references.text: Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold, which demonstrates his ability to weigh out 400 shekels of silver for the cave of Machpelah.
Abraham offers to pay the full price for the field – verse 16 describes the actual execution of the payment.
Isaac and Ishmael bury Abraham in the cave of Machpelah, which he purchased from Ephron the Hittite – the transaction described in 23:16.
Jacob describes the cave of Machpelah as the burial place for the patriarchs, specifying that Abraham bought the field and the cave from Ephron the Hittite.
Jacob's sons bury him in the cave of Machpelah on the field that Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
Jeremiah weighs out silver when buying a field in Anathoth – a parallel to Abraham weighing out silver ('silver current among merchants') when purchasing the cave of Machpelah.

Both verses are parts of the same legal transaction where Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah, and they intertwine the public witness testimony with the actual payment to emphasize the validity of the purchase.
